 J U D G M E N T
This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .25,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by her in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 13.11.2022 at around 03.00 a.m., when she was traveling as a passenger in KSRTC Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-13-F-2308 from Hassan towards Kunigal, near Jnanabharathi School, Kunigal Town, the said KSRTC Bus, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and run across the bus at road humps.

As a result, petitioner Mangala vs K S R T C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109374952/
1 fell down from her seat and sustained grievous injuries.

sentences.text:
Thereafter, the petitioner was shifted to M.
M. Hospital, Kunigal and later to General Hospital, Channapatana, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .1,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was earning .20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of KSRTC Bus by its driver.
The respondent being the owner is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In pursuance of notice, the respondent appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed written statement.
4. In the written statement, the respondent has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.

The respondent also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place,
time and manner of accident.
Further respondent contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further contended that at the time of alleged accident, the bus is on scheduled trip from Subramanya to Bengaluru and was being driven by its driver on the left side of road by observing all the traffic rules and regulations and while it was so proceeding in Kunigal near Ghanbharthi school road humps, the Autorickshaw, which was proceeding ahead of the bus, abruptly stopped the autorickshaw, due to darkness and invisibility of humps, in front of the bus without giving any signal and the driver of bus also stopped the bus.
When the things stood thus, the petitioner who was sleeping in the seat, due to drowsiness fell down from the bus, but not sustained any injuries.
There is no negligence on the part of driver of KSRTC bus in the cause of accident.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of KSRTC Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-13-F-2308 by its driver, in RTA took place on 13.11.2022 at about 03.00 p.m., on infront of Jnanabharathi School, NH-75, Kunigal Yadiyuru Main Road, Kunigal Town,
Tumkuru?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What order or award?

6. In order to prove the contention of the petition, the petitioner examined herself as PW.1, got examined Dr.Ramesh.B., working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru as PW.2 Mangala vs K S R T C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109374952/
2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11 and closed evidence of her side.

On the other hand,
the driver of KSRTC Bus got examined as RW.1 and no documents have been marked on his behalf and closed evidence of respondent side.

7. Heard arguments of both side and perused the materials available on record.
8.

Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are under:-
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative;
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative; Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:-

9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner contended that on 13.11.2022 at about 03.00 a.m., accident occurred in front of Jananabharthi School, Kunigal-Yadiyuru Road, Kunigal Town, while she was traveling in KSRTC Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-13-F-2308, due to the rash and negligent driving of the above said bus by its driver in which she sustained grievous injuries.
10.
Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced Ex.P2, first information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P2, first information statement, the husband of petitioner by name Sri.
Chikkaveeraiah S/o Late Naganna has lodged complaint with police on 18.11.2022 pertaining to accident occurred on 13.11.2022.
The police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Ex . P1
discloses the aspect of registration of FIR against the driver of offending KSRTC Bus.
The petitioner also furnished spot mahazar, which is marked as Ex.P.3.
The said document discloses that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said document.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Ex.P.6 is the Wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the accident.
Ex.P.5 is the IMV Report which indicates the aspect of seizure of bus by the police and inspecting the same through the concerned official.
The bus will be seized by the police on the ground of its involvement in the accident.
The respondent does not appear to have questioned the seizure procedure conducted by the police before concerned authority.
The said document indicates the involvement of the bus in the cause of accident.

The I.O.,
after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC as per Ex.P.7.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The respondent does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondent to show that the investigation is not conducted in proper manner.
The respondent does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report,
the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle Mangala vs K S R T C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109374952/

sentences.text: which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondent not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioner could be elicited.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioner pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
11. Further, on perusal of the materials, there appears to be delay of 5 days in lodging first information statement.
The accident occurred on 13.11.2022.
As per Ex.P.1, first information statement, husband of petitioner has lodged a complaint with police on 18.11.2022.
As per the materials placed on record, there was five days delay in lodging complaint.
The complainant in his complaint explained that he was in hospital along with the petitioner while she was taking treatment as an inpatient and thereafter lodged the complaint with the police.
Further, on perusal of hospital documents placed by the petitioner, it discloses that immediately after the accident, the petitioner was taken to the hospital.
In general parlance, the injured as well as his family members think about providing best treatment to the patient rather than to lodge complaint before the police.
Only on the ground of delay in lodging complaint the claim cannot be doubted and the case cannot be dismissed.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Ravi Vs. Badrinarayana in (2011) 4 SCC 693, held that delay in lodging a FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimants case.
In view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, this tribunal cannot dismiss the petition only on the ground of delay in lodging the complaint.
No materials are placed to create doubt about contention of petitioner related to accident and negligence of respondent in the cause of accident.
Merely because there is delay in lodging the first information statement, the case of the petitioner cannot be considered to be doubtful.
12. On the other hand, the driver of KSRTC Bus got examined as RW.1.
The evidence of RW.1 discloses the aspect of occurrence of accident.
Though RW.1 denied the aspect of negligence on his part in the cause of accident, no substantive materials are placed in order to prove the same.
No satisfactory materials are placed by respondent in order to disprove the contention of petitioner.
The respondent not furnished satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to accident and negligence of driver of KSRTC bus.
The evidence of RW.1 is not of much assistance to the respondent in disproving or rebutting the contention of petitioner related to accident and negligence of driver of KSRTC bus.
13. The respondent not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondent not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of record, it discloses that accident was caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.7, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of KSRTC Bus bearing Regn.No.KA-13-F-2308 by its driver and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Mangala vs K S R T C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109374952/

Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:
The petitioner succeeded in establishing that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of KSRTC Bus vehicle.

As Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

The Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury,
pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc., in order to assess the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled.
i) Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident she sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.
In order to prove the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner produced Wound certificate issued by M.M. Multispeciality Hospital marked at Ex.P.6.
The said document discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner and that the injuries are grievous in nature.
The petitioner also furnished Ex.P.9, discharge card, which discloses the aspect of availing treatment by petitioner for the injuries sustained by her in the accident.
Further, the petitioner examined Dr.Ramesh.B as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P10 & 11 documents.
PW.2/doctor deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of permanent physical disability to the right lower limb at 20% and to whole body at 10%.
On consideration of the materials placed before the Tribunal, compensation of .50,000/- appears just and reasonable towards Pain and Suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:- The petitioner has not produced any medical bills to show that she has taken treatment at the hospital.
The petitioner not furnished any materials in order to show the expenses incurred by her for the treatment of injuries.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the petitioner cannot be considered to be entitled to compensation towards medical expenses.
As such petitioner is not entitled for compensation towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:- On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 13.11.2023 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital.
On perusal of materials on record, the petitioner appears to have admitted as an inpatient at Hospital pertaining to the injuries sustained by her and availed treatment as an inpatient.
So, during the time of treatment the petitioner might have required good food and extra nourishment.

PW.2/Doctor has produced Ex.P.9, Discharge Card issued by General Hospital, Channapatana, which discloses the aspect of availing treatment by petitioner as an inpatient from 13.11.2022 to 17.11.2022 i.e., for a period of 05 days.

Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .500/- per day for 05 days to a sum of .2,500/-
appears just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.

(iv) Towards Conveyance:-

sentences.text: The petitioner is the resident of Rajivgandhinagara, Idga Layout, Tumkur Taluk, Tumkur District and she has admitted to hospital for treatment.
In order to prove this aspect the petitioner has produced discharge card marked at Ex.P.9.
The petitioner might have incurred expenses for conveyance during the period of treatment.

Considering the injuries sustained and facts of the case,
the tribunal is of view that the compensation of .10,000/- appears just and proper towards conveyance charges.

(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:-
The petitioner contended that she was self-employee and earning a sum of .20,000/- per month.
In order to prove the income, the petitioner not produced any documents.
The petitioner not furnished materials to show that she was earning .20,000/- per month.
No materials are furnished by petitioner in order to substantiate her contention that she is earning .20,000/- per month.
The petitioner not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to substantiate her contention regarding occupation and income.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional income is to be taken into consideration.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner considered as .15,500/-.
On perusal of record, it appears that petitioner might have not attended her work for some time due to accidental injuries.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .20,000/- towards loss of income during treatment.

(vi) Towards Loss of future earning capacity:-
The petitioner has contended that due to accident, she was admitted as an inpatient at Hospital and sustained permanent disablement.
The petitioner also examined Dr.Ramesh.B working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru as PW.2.
PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.
The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained fracture of right patella and underwent internal fixation of Patella later underwent removal of implants.
Further petitioner complains of pain in right knee, difficulty to squat on floor, sit cross legged, climb upstairs, walk on slope, kneel, difficulty to do routine activities.
Further PW.2 deposed in his chief examination, that as per radiological examination fractures are united.
The doctor has assessed the disability to the right lower limb at 20% and to the whole body at 10%.

In order to prove his disability, the doctor has produced OPD record and X-rays marked at Ex.P.10 &
11.
PW.2 not stated that the petitioner could not be able to do her routine activities in a normal way.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the petitioner to show that the petitioner is unable to do any work at all.
The injuries sustained by petitioner do not appear to cause much problem in doing her activities.

As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay Kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability is assessed at 05%.

sentences.text: In order to prove age of the petitioner, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.8 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card, wherein her date of birth is shown as 01.01.1977.
The accident occurred on 13.11.2022.
As per the materials placed on record, the age of petitioner appears to 46 years at the time of accident.
The respondent not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the document furnished by petitioner related to her.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the document furnished by petitioner is to be considered for ascertaining the age.
As per the document furnished by petitioner, her age is 46 years as on the date of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier.
As per Smt.Sarla Verma case multiplier applicable is '13'.

As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay Kumar and another,
this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of her gross income.

sentences.text:
Hence, future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Annual Income before accident : (.15,500/- x 12) = .1,86,000/-
 Loss of future earning p.a. (05% of prior annual  income) = .9,300/-.
Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 13 Loss of future earnings - (.9,300/- x 13) = .1,20,900/-.
The petitioner is entitled for .1,20,900/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
(vii) Deprivation of Future Amenities:-
The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and she is unable to do her day- today activities as earlier.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.

So, the respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

18. Issue No.3:-

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .2,13,400/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Thirteen Thousand Four Hundred only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.

Respondent is the owner of the  offending vehicle is liable to pay the  compensation to the petitioner and to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as amount is meager one.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.
